title: Long META — Q2 Earnings Catalyst + ISM Expansion Confirms Ad-Spend Cycle Acceleration
entry: Long $563–578 at market (META at ~$572 on July 1, lifted by XLC sector strength on ISM expansion day). Entry is available at current levels; do not chase above $585 — above that level the pre-earnings premium has exceeded the first target band and the risk/reward compresses before the July 29 catalyst. Scale: 70% initial on July 1–2; 30% add on any pullback to $555–562 if offered post-NFP (a Goldilocks NFP scenario would sustain the XLC bid and create an add opportunity). Size 4% of gross.
stop_loss: $538 daily close (~5.9% below $572) — implies either (1) NFP July 2 prints below 80K, signaling labor market deterioration that historically precedes advertiser budget cuts and directly threatens the Q2 ad-revenue guide; (2) META pre-announces a Q2 revenue miss below $57B, or management withdraws the $58–61B Q2 guidance; or (3) SPX closes below 7,300 (BEARISH regime escalation) compressing growth multiples across large-cap internet. A close at $538 would represent the first close below the Q1 2026 post-earnings lows and invalidates the recovery thesis entirely.
targets: $600 — Q2 earnings beat on July 29: revenue above $61B high end of guidance + ad impressions +20% YoY; Llama 4-based ad optimization materializes in CPM data; management raises Q3 revenue guidance above $64B; first target exit 40% of position; +4.9% from $572 midpoint

$640 — Q3 guidance upgrade cycle begins: sell-side consensus Q3 estimates revised from ~$63B to $65–67B; AI inference efficiency metric first disclosed (revenue-per-compute-unit improving); multiple re-rates from post-CapEx concern lows toward the pre-Q1 correction levels; exit 40%; +11.9%

$685 — Full re-rating on AI monetization visibility: Q4 2026 preliminary ad-demand commentary signals a third consecutive quarter of double-digit impression growth; annual CapEx is absorbed as a positive (infrastructure moat), not a negative; META trades at 28–30x forward earnings vs current 25x; exit final 20%; +19.8%
catalyst: Meta Platforms reports Q2 2026 earnings on July 29, 2026 after market close. The company guided Q2 revenue of $58–61B — implying 22–29% YoY growth — in its April Q1 report. Q1 2026 showed $56.31B revenue (+33% YoY), with ad impressions growing 19% and average price per ad rising 12%. The post-Q1 selloff was driven by an 8% CapEx guidance increase to $114–125B for 2026. The opportunity now is that the market punished the CapEx surprise but has not yet credited the returns: Llama 4-based ad optimization (running since Q4 2025) is compounding in Q2, while the June 2026 ISM Manufacturing expansion (54.0, 37-month high) confirms the corporate ad-spend recovery cycle that META's guidance has been implicitly projecting.
thesis:
Meta enters the Q2 earnings window with three reinforcing tailwinds converging on the July 29 catalyst. First, the ad-spend cycle is expanding. ISM Manufacturing June 2026 printed 54.0 — the sixth consecutive month above 50, a 37-month high, and a beat versus consensus 53.0. Manufacturing expansion historically leads to advertising demand recovery with a 4–6 month lag as CEO confidence translates to incremental marketing budget allocation. With ISM at 54.0 in June (and the prior reading in May also above 52), the lagged signal implies Q3 ad-spend demand should accelerate beyond what META's current Q2 guidance captures. The July 29 call is the first opportunity for management to articulate this demand acceleration in forward guidance.

Second, the AI monetization return on CapEx has not been credited. The Q1 2026 selloff was driven entirely by the $114–125B CapEx guidance increase — the market read this as margin compression without specifying the return. But META's Llama 4 models are running in production across Instagram Reels recommendation, WhatsApp ad targeting, and Facebook feed optimization since Q4 2025. The first full two-quarter look at Llama 4 efficiency will be the Q2 report: if CPM improvement data is disclosed (revenue per ad impression improving faster than cost per serving), the CapEx overhang becomes a moat rather than a liability. At ~25x forward earnings, META is cheap versus its own history if the AI return thesis validates.

Third, sector mechanics are constructive. XLC is leading the July 1 session as the Dow inclusion bid drives institutional buying across Communication Services. META is the second-largest XLC constituent. The ISM expansion narrative, the GOOGL Dow rebalancing tail, and the broad AI capex investment cycle are simultaneously lifting XLC — creating a sector tailwind on top of the idiosyncratic Q2 earnings setup. The three-week pre-earnings window (July 1–July 29) historically sees institutional positioning build in the week ahead of large-cap tech results.

The counter-party argues: the Q1 post-earnings selloff happened despite a revenue beat, suggesting the multiple is structurally capped at current CapEx levels. A weak NFP tomorrow would threaten the ad-spend narrative directly — advertisers respond rapidly to labor market deterioration. EU Digital Services Act enforcement (targeting META's AI training data on European user data) remains a regulatory wildcard. The $114–125B CapEx guide could be revised upward again on July 29, triggering a second round of margin concern selling regardless of the revenue line.
bull_case: Q2 revenue of $62–63B (above the $61B high end of guidance) with ad impressions +22% YoY. Management discloses first efficiency metric on AI ad optimization (e.g., CPM improvement +8% attributable to Llama 4). Q3 guidance issued above $64B. CapEx concerns absorbed as buy-side builds multi-year AI return model. META to $640 (Target 2) within 2 weeks of the July 29 report. Full re-rate to $685 (Target 3) if Q4 guidance is also raised on the October earnings call — compounding the July 29 catalyst with a second beat-and-raise cycle.
bear_case: NFP July 2 prints hot (>150K, wages +0.4%), triggering the BofA 3-hike path. Advertiser budgets get repriced lower as real consumer spending models are revised. META pre-Q2-earnings channel checks (published by Bernstein, KeyBanc) signal ad-spend deceleration in June. Q2 revenue lands at $58–59B (low end of guidance), perceived as a miss versus elevated expectations after the ISM-driven setup. CapEx is again revised upward (to $130B+). Stock re-tests $540 stop on a pre-earnings guide-down narrative.
invalidation: $538 daily close; OR NFP July 2 prints below 80K (recession signal — direct negative for ad-spend guidance); OR META announces a formal EU DSA consent decree that caps AI training data usage across the EU (structural revenue impairment); OR SPX closes below 7,300 (BEARISH regime — growth multiples compress across the board); OR July 1 ISM Prices Paid confirmed above 85.0 (embedded inflation) causing rate-hike repricing that compresses Nasdaq P/E toward 24x and directly limits META's multiple.
